title: Relations and Functions: Equivalence Relations, One-one and Onto Functions
seo_title: Relations and Functions Class 12 Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 1)
standard_text: Types of relations: reflexive, symmetric, transitive and equivalence relations; one to one and onto functions (summary of the CBSE syllabus)
meta_desc: Class 12 Relations and Functions worksheet (NCERT Chapter 1): reflexive, symmetric and transitive relations, equivalence classes, one-one, onto and bijective functions, and counting functions. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: One-one: different inputs, different outputs. Onto: every element of the co-domain is an image.
body_html:
How it works

  • R on A is reflexive if (a, a) ∈ R for every a; symmetric if (a, b) ∈ R ⇒ (b, a) ∈ R; transitive if (a, b), (b, c) ∈ R ⇒ (a, c) ∈ R.
  • An equivalence relation has all three. It splits A into disjoint equivalence classes.
  • f is one-one if f(x1) = f(x2) ⇒ x1 = x2; onto if every element of the co-domain has a pre-image; bijective if both.
  • From a set of m elements to one of n elements: nm functions, nPm one-one functions (m ≤ n).
Example

Is R = {(a, b) : a ≤ b} on Z an equivalence relation?

Reflexive: a ≤ a, yes

Symmetric: 1 ≤ 2 but not 2 ≤ 1, no

Transitive: yes

Answer: No, it is not symmetric

Common mistakes

  • Calling a relation reflexive when one pair (a, a) is missing.
  • Saying f(x) = x² on R is one-one.
  • Thinking a one-one function must be onto when the sets are infinite.

faq.a: Yes. A function has an inverse exactly when it is one-one and onto.
Yes; there are no pairs to break the rule.

items.q: R = {(a, b) : |a − b| is a multiple of 3} on A = {0, 1, 2, …, 12}. Find the equivalence class [0].

items.q: f : R → R, f(x) = 2x + 5. Which is true?
items.e: One-one: different inputs give different outputs. Onto: every element of the co-domain is an image. So f is one-one and onto (bijective).

items.q: f : R → R, f(x) = x². Which is true?
items.e: One-one: two different inputs give the same output. Onto: some element of the co-domain is not an image. So f is neither one-one nor onto.

items.q: A has 4 elements and B has 3 elements. How many one-one functions are there from A to B?
items.e: A one-one function needs at least as many elements in B as in A. Here 4 > 3, so there are 0.

items.q: A has 3 elements and B has 5 elements. How many functions are there from A to B?
items.e: Each of the 3 elements of A has 5 choices: 53 = 125.
